value.quote: So we have a rather complete characterization of equilibria, or at least
value.note: Main results: existence, limit points, stability of turnout equilibria and Jury/non-Jury theorems at equilibrium limits; Sec. 6.1 adds a numerical simulation on a synthetic example (Example 5). Winning probability of the better candidate is analysed as a property of equilibria, not as performance against a welfare/distortion objective (consistent with C5.1 = N).

C1.reason: Types EQ and SI as A coded; WD is not warranted because the Jury results characterise equilibrium win probabilities rather than welfare or distortion, consistent with the agreed C5.1 = N.

value.note: Bayes-Nash equilibrium for the Calculus of Voting; 'election equilibrium' with heuristic perceived pivotality models (BND); stability of equilibria (Theorem 9) is defined via simultaneous best-response dynamics converging to the equilibrium (App. D, Def. 11) (ITER).

C8.1.reason: Stability, a main result, is defined through best-response dynamics ('a best response by few agents will get closer to Q... until convergence'), so ITER applies in addition to BNE and BND.
